sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.8% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, reaching $31.7 billion [F198][F9].
Operating income grew faster, at 5.8% a year, lifting operating margin from 22.9% to 27.2% [F199][F20][F28].
FY2022 was the step change, with revenue up 17.1% on rate cases, favorable weather and volumes [D239][P26][P33].
FY2020 was the trough, when operating income fell 19.9% on coal ash settlement charges and pandemic-driven volume losses [D156][P60].
Electric Utilities and Infrastructure supplied 90.9% of FY2025 revenue and 3.6pp of the 5.6% growth [D541][D543][D358].
Residential electric was the largest customer class at 43.3% of revenue, contributing 2.8pp of FY2025 growth [D774][D776].
Gas Utilities and Infrastructure grew 27.1% in FY2025, adding 2.0pp, with Piedmont Natural Gas up 32.1% [D565][D566][D682].
Operating income grew 8.8% against 5.6% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 41.4% [D359][D358][D378].
Diluted EPS rose 10.5% against 9.8% net income growth as the diluted share count rose 0.6% [D362][D360][D374].
FY2025 operating margin of 27.2% is the window high, 4.3pp above the 22.9% median and 7.5pp above the FY2020 low [F28][D932][D933][D931].
The FY2025 margin rose 0.8pp as revenue growth outpaced operating-cost growth by only 0.3pp [D370][D379].
D&A reached 24.3% of revenue in FY2025, up from 21.4% in FY2024, the main drag on the margin [D341][D303].
Net margin of 15.7% sits below the 17.6% peer median, a 25th-percentile result, despite the 75th-percentile operating margin [F47][D952][D951][D949].
Interest expense rose to $3.6 billion in FY2025 on higher outstanding debt balances and rates [X63][P10].
Operating cash flow of $12.3 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, against 3.48x in FY2023 [F77][F38][D346][D268].
Free cash flow was negative $1.7 billion, a -5.3% margin, against a -5.8% window median [F97][D343][D939].
Capex of $14.0 billion was 44.2% of revenue and 1.82x D&A, so capital spending alone exceeds operating cash flow [F87][D342][D348].
FY2022 conversion broke down to a -19.0% free-cash-flow margin as rising fuel costs drove undercollections and higher borrowings [D223][P36].
Net cash stood at -$89.6 billion in FY2025, or -282.3% of revenue, versus a -228.4% peer median, a 25th-percentile position [D352][D353][D954][D953].
Total debt grew 6.6% in FY2025 while cash fell 22.0% to $245 million, and the current ratio slipped to 0.55x [D376][D375][F137][F177].
Return on average equity of 9.7% ranks at the 0th percentile against a 12.6% peer median [D357][D955][D956].
Dividends of $3.2 billion were paid in FY2022, the last year disclosed, and the diluted share count rose from 691 million to 777 million over the window [X122][X106][X115].
The current ratio fell to 0.55x in FY2025, below 1.0x and near the 0.53x window low [F177][D943].
Cash and investments cover only 0.1 years of the latest $1.7 billion burn [D356][D355].
Net cash has fallen for nine straight years, from -$50.0 billion in FY2016 to -$89.6 billion in FY2025 [D14][D352][R3].
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in each of FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 [D269][D309][D347][R4].
FY2021 operating expenses, pretax income and tax were later restated, so FY2021 comparisons use first-reported values [X29][X69][X79][R6].
If FY2026 operating margin falls back toward the 22.9% window median from 27.2%, the margin expansion trend has reversed [D933][F28].
Free cash flow staying below the -5.8% window median margin would keep net cash falling from -$89.6 billion [D939][D352].
A current ratio recovering above the 0.66x window median would ease the liquidity flag from 0.55x [D945][F177].
